reason: The counted theorem requires one geometric construction to satisfy four interacting conditions: arbitrarily small p-independence, sparse inner graphs, an arbitrary rational cross density, and a sharp mixed-clique exclusion when ell<=p/2. The core is not supplied by sphere concentration: it requires coherent root-of-unity rotation labels, a buffered complex phase window compatible with discretization, and a convex-hull/far-rotation argument whose imaginary-part lower bound contradicts a product of two small vector norms. These are research-level construction and obstruction mechanisms beyond routine qualifying-exam use of concentration or Caratheodory. I independently support H3 for the full selected chain, with the source qualifications below explicitly disclosed.

Each part is a tagged copy of the sample, even if representatives at the same location are chosen.
small_p_independence: 820–865: remove at most p−1 bad rotation sets using the two-set cap consequence, find rotated points near one common unit vector by the parallelogram law, then pass to cell representatives with diameter mu/4. The final norm bound also forces the chosen representatives to be distinct, by the same nonzero-root separation.
density_and_discretization: 881–940: rotational invariance gives uniform phase measure; cap bounds remove p thin imaginary strips at cost O(epsilon*K*p), and the contracted phase window costs O(K^(-1/2)). Inner-product perturbation at most mu/4 retains a K*mu imaginary margin and controls phase displacement. The omitted upper degree estimate uses the same perturbation estimate in reverse and the enlarged phase interval, with no new concentration theorem or new graph construction.
mixed_clique_exclusion: 948–988: coherent rotation labels give a far pair in Y; the sufficiently large label set of X has0 in its convex hull, so a convex combination of at most3 selected vertices has norm<=sqrt(mu). Pairing it with y−rho^m y-prime has imaginary part<=mu by Cauchy–Schwarz, whereas the phase window and all rotated imaginary margins force>=2Kmu.
parameter_and_count_scope: Choose K large, epsilon sufficiently small relative to K,p, then k sufficiently large including epsilon*sqrt(k) tending to infinity; n subsequently meets the partition bound. Diagonal choices give the stated little-o quantities for every sufficiently large n. There are2n total vertices, hence the cross density ell/p produces the lower bound ell/(2p) in Ramsey–Turan density. The historical conjecture is not assumed; only its explicit varrho-star formula is evaluated.

approved_task_config.difficulty_reason: The counted result is the full construction, not a local triangle-inequality lemma. It must make four competing global properties hold at once: asymptotically prescribed rational cross density, vanishing inner density, sublinear p-independence, and a sharp forbidden mixed clique. The new mechanism is the coupling of root-of-unity near-rotations to a complex phase window; the final mixed-clique obstruction combines planar convexity with a signed imaginary-part estimate. Standard concentration bounds alone provide none of this construction. H3 is a provisional initial assessment requiring two independent substantive reviews of this same complete unit.
